title: Streaming interrupt coordinator and time-window heuristics for Go SDK
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: the current Go SDK streaming implementation lacks a unified approach to negotiating time windows and behavioral semantics between clients and the Redwood streaming runtime. This causes race conditions during cancel/timeout races, inconsistent backpressure handling when the process is suspended (e.g., container preemption), and confusing retry behavior when partial payloads are emitted before an interrupt.

Goal: implement an interrupt coordinator and a small set of heuristics for "time-window negotiation" that makes streaming cancellation, per-message deadlines, and suspend/resume behavior deterministic and easy for application developers to reason about. The coordinator is a client-side abstraction that mediates: (1) deadline propagation from callers into the stream, (2) cooperative preemption notifications from the runtime (suspend/evict), and (3) graceful drain vs force-close policies for shutdown.

Scope: Go SDK only (client library), compatibility with existing server-side behavior is required. This ticket covers design, API surface, reference implementation, unit tests, and integration test with the streaming test harness. Rollout will be behind an opt-in flag for 1.6.0.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New InterruptCoordinator type added to Go SDK that exposes: Start(ctx), Interrupt(reason string), Suspend(timeout time.Duration), Resume(), and Status() (enum string).
2) When a caller passes a ctx with deadline into StreamReceive(ctx, ...), the coordinator must ensure that per-message reads respect the strongest applicable deadline (caller ctx deadline vs per-message deadline header) and returns a well-documented error (StreamCanceled / StreamDeadline) when exceeded.
3) Suspend() causes in-flight reads to return quickly with a well-defined transient error (StreamSuspended) and sets a reconnect hint for sdks to attempt exponential backoff reconnection.
4) Resume() restores normal read semantics; outstanding idempotency guarantees are recorded in metrics.
5) Library-level examples showing idiomatic cancellation and graceful drain.
6) Integration tests in streaming-harness proving suspend/resume and deadline races under synthetic load.
7) Documentation page and migration guide published to docs site.
8) No regressions on existing streaming tests (all green).
design_decisions:
- Keep the coordinator local to the SDK rather than pushing a new protocol to the server—this reduces rollout risk and allows server-side hints to be consumed opportunistically via headers.
- Use a small, deterministic enum for interruption outcomes: StreamOK, StreamTimeout, StreamCanceled, StreamSuspended, StreamInterrupted. Use these strings in error types to make error handling deterministic across users.
- Prefer explicit Suspend()/Resume() signals to lazy timeouts for container preemption; runtime will send a short-lived suspend hint header that the SDK converts into Suspend() with a default 10s window.
- Backpressure heuristic: when the client detects slow consumer (read call blocked > 2x mean RTT), the coordinator will switch to a single-item read window and enable aggressive KV-prefix caching to reduce load. This is a best-effort optimization that can be disabled via StreamOptions.
- Retries: only allow resumable retries for idempotent ops; non-idempotent streams are closed and an error is returned. A resumable checkpoint token is exposed on the stream handle for the application to persist if they want stronger resume semantics.
implementation_notes:
- Add new file pkg/streaming/coordinator.go implementing InterruptCoordinator (no external deps).
- Modify StreamRecv(ctx, opts) to accept an optional Coordinator parameter in StreamOptions. Backwards compatible: if nil, default coordinator is used.
- Error types implemented as variables with sentinel strings: ErrStreamTimeout, ErrStreamCanceled, ErrStreamSuspended, ErrStreamInterrupted. They implement errors.Is via errors.As wrappers to support comparisons.
- Metrics: streaming.interrupt.suspend_count, streaming.interrupt.resume_count, streaming.interrupt.suspend_latency_ms, streaming.read.window_size, streaming.resumable.checkpoint_emitted.
- Tests: unit tests for coordinator state machine; fuzz tests for deadline edge cases; integration test in streaming-harness simulating server suspend header and verifying reconnect/backoff.
- Provide an example in examples/streaming/graceful_drain.go and examples/streaming/suspend_resume_test.go.
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk/pull/789 (WIP).
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: users depend on previous indefinite read semantics; adding agressive suspend semantics may surface new errors. Mitigation: opt-in flag and prominent migration docs with code examples.
- Risk: introducing default heuristics could hide root cause of slow consumers. Mitigation: heuristics are disabled by default; add SDK env var REDWOOD_SDK_STREAMING_HEURISTICS=on for dogfooding.
- Risk: checkpoint tokens leak sensitive info. Mitigation: checkpoint token is opaque base64 and can be configured to be no-op; docs call out sensitivity and recommend KMS if persisted.
- Risk: metric cardinality explosion from per-stream labels. Mitigation: limit label dimensions to small fixed set (route, model, region).
test_plan:
- Unit tests: coordinator state transitions (Start->Suspend->Resume->Interrupt).
- Edge-case tests: ctx deadline < per-message deadline; ctx canceled mid-read; server suspend header arrives during backlog drain.
- Integration: streaming-harness scenario that: (1) opens N concurrent streams, (2) triggers suspend header on half of them, (3) asserts those streams return ErrStreamSuspended and the SDK attempts reconnect with exponential backoff, (4) after Resume event, stream re-establishes without data duplication for idempotent payloads.
- Performance: run slow consumer scenario (1k qps aggregate) and assert no >10% regression in median latency.
- Fuzz: random cancel/timeout sequences for 10k iterations to find races.
- e2e: light smoke test on hosted API to ensure compatibility.
deployment_notes:
- Feature gated behind environment variable REDWOOD_GO_SDK_INTERRUPT_COORDINATOR=true and StreamOptions.EnableCoordinator=true.
- Rollout plan: enable for internal dogfood (redwood-internal) for 1 week, then opt-in beta for select customers, then default enable in go-sdk-1.7.0 if telemetry is healthy.
- Rollback: env var off or revert to previous default coordinator (no-op) if >1% error increase detected in streaming errors telemetry within 24 hours.
- Monitoring: dashboard draft created at Grafana link in related_links; alert streams.errors.rate > 0.5% triggers page.
